## Claims
- [computed] For \(c=6\), accepted artifact `162283c7d25bcc9b6cf77717e180ce1c85e4bdcbe2d0dbabc186aab75e18d126` records
  \[
  (\operatorname{rank}Q_d)_{d=4}^{8}=(1,1,2,1,1),
  \quad Q_d=0\ (9\le d\le32),
  \]
  with no torsion in every recorded degree.
- [proved] Hence
  \[
  Q\cong \mathbb Z^{1+1+2+1+1}=\mathbb Z^6.
  \]
- [proved] Relative to accepted generation of
  \[
  G_L=\{\bar s_\mu:2^2\subseteq\mu\subseteq2^4\},\qquad
  G_R=\{\bar s_\mu:2^2\subseteq\mu\subseteq4^2\},
  \]
  each six-element family maps onto \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^6\). The accepted indexed-family Nakayama criterion therefore makes each image a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(Q\), so neither \(G_L\) nor \(G_R\) has a removable generator.
- [proved] The requested \(i=j=p=2,\ c=6\) minimality corollary is established relative to the accepted computation dependency and accepted generation criterion; no parent-theorem claim is made.

## Strategy
Summed the accepted degreewise ranks:
\[
1+1+2+1+1=6.
\]
A surjection \(\mathbb Z^6\twoheadrightarrow Q\cong\mathbb Z^6\) is an isomorphism. Thus deletion of any member leaves a family whose images cannot generate \(Q\), hence cannot generate \(J_v\). No new sandbox artifact was produced; this certificate uses the identified accepted artifact.
